name: sit-bug
reply:
Root cause found for the webhook retry incident: the retry counter lived on the request object, and the queue rebuilt that object on every 5xx response, so the counter went back to zero each time. A failing endpoint was retried forever (we saw attempt 40 in the logs) and the dead-letter alert never fired.

The flow was: send the webhook, the endpoint answers 5xx, the worker rebuilds the request, then it checks the attempt limit. The rebuild step wiped the count before the check ran, so the limit of five was never reached.

The fix moves the counter onto the job record in the database, so it survives the rebuild. The worker now stops after five attempts, marks the job dead and sends one alert. Verified with a test that fails an endpoint on purpose: before the change it retried more than 40 times in a minute, now it makes exactly 5 attempts and stops. Old rows that were already stuck were closed by hand.
